# How this pipeline works

Every workflow here is generated from `hollow.yml`. To change the pipeline, change `hollow.yml` and run `npx the-hollow upgrade`. `npx the-hollow fix` explains a failing run (and repairs it, if you configured a model), and `npx the-hollow doctor` checks the whole setup.

## On every pull request

`ci.yml` runs these jobs, and the `CI passed` check sums them up for branch protection:

- **Build and test:** installs from the lockfile (`uv sync --locked`), then runs:
  - Lint: `uv run --no-sync ruff check .`
  - Format check: `uv run --no-sync ruff format --check .`
  - Type check: `uv run --no-sync mypy .`
  - Test: `uv run --no-sync pytest`
  - the alembic migrations, applied to a throwaway database
- **Secret scan:** Gitleaks over the whole git history.
- **Dependency scan:** OSV-Scanner on the lockfiles; fails on high or worse.
- **SAST:** CodeQL on public repos, Semgrep on private ones.
- **Container:** builds the image and scans it with Trivy.

`pr-title.yml` requires a Conventional Commit title, since squash merges turn it into the changelog.

`migrations.yml` (the `Migration safety` check) fails on destructive migrations unless the pull request has the `allow-destructive-migration` label. See docs/migrations.md.

## Releases and deploys

`release.yml` deploys to a container image on GHCR. Every merge to `main` deploys to staging. release-please keeps a release pull request open; merging it tags a version and promotes the exact build staging ran to production, which waits for approval. Nothing is rebuilt on the way.

Production waits for the `production` environment's required reviewers. Where GitHub offers none (private repos without Enterprise), the release stops before production, and someone with write access approves it by running the Release workflow with the version: `gh workflow run release.yml -f version=v1.2.3`.

| Environment | URL | Deploys |
|---|---|---|
| staging | (set in hollow.yml) | on every merge |
| production | (set in hollow.yml) | on release |

After each deploy, the environment's URL plus `/` must answer without a server error within two minutes.

Each deploy applies the database migrations before its new code goes live. See docs/migrations.md.

## Rolling back

Each environment is a tag (`:staging`, `:production`) on the image. A failed health check moves the tag back to the previous digest automatically. To roll back by hand, run the Release workflow with an earlier version: it deploys that release's own image.

## Secrets and variables

`npx the-hollow secrets` lists which are set and offers to set the missing ones. Values never go in a file.

| Name | Kind | Where | Needed | What for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL` | secret | staging environment | yes | staging's database URL, so its deploy applies migrations first |
| `DATABASE_URL` | secret | production environment | yes | production's database URL, so its deploy applies migrations first |
| `RELEASE_PLEASE_TOKEN` | secret | repo | optional | token release-please uses, so CI runs on release pull requests |

## Scheduled checks and incidents


Every night it re-scans the default branch's dependencies, since new vulnerabilities are published without any code changing.

A failing synthetic check, nightly scan or production deploy raises an incident issue labelled `hollow-incident`. Repeats add a comment instead of a new issue, and the issue closes itself once the check passes again.
